    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

    Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the significant positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

    Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

    Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the fresh year.

    Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

    Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

    His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

    According to recent reports, emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

    It has been revealed that “Of course there is still work to do but they indicated they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

    This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another vital player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

    England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

    While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

    Recent findings suggest that the Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

    Recent findings suggest that hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

    The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

    Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

    Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

    According to recent reports, it was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

    Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

    Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

    In a recent development, PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

    Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

    Sources indicate that villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

    The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

    It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

    PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

    It has been revealed that after the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

    PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK.

    In a recent development, both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

    Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the newly introduced Premier League season.

    PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

    Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

    In a recent development, not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

    PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo.

    Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

    Into the final minute of added time we go.

    Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

    There will be five added minutes.

    Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

    Industry observers note that one final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

    Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

    Industry observers note that the ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

    Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

    Recent findings suggest that alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

    PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

    Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

    The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

    We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

    According to recent reports, aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a substantial chance for Hemmings.

    Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

    The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given.     Recent findings suggest that two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

    Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

    In a recent development, after one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

    On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

    Recent findings suggest that aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

    Sources indicate that the Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

    Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a major summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

    “I feel like the club is in a latest era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

    Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

    In a recent development, PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

    “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

    Sources indicate that “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

    According to recent reports, PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

    Micah Parsons injury update: Packers star cleared to make 2026 debut vs. Rams in Week 12

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Green Bay Packers (6-4) are coming out of their Week 11 bye week with a major boost: the return of All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons.
    • "I would say I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday but for sure this season," Parsons said on Monday, via ESPN.
    • Parsons suffered multiple knee injuries, a torn ACL and meniscus, in last season's Week 15 loss at the Denver Broncos.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Green Bay Packers (6-4) are coming out of their Week 11 bye week with a major boost: the return of All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons. The five-time Pro Bowler was reportedly cleared to make his 2026 NFL season debut in Week 12 at the Los Angeles Rams (6-4) on Wednesday night, according to ESPN.

    "I would say I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday but for sure this season," Parsons said on Monday, via ESPN. "And I'll be looking forward to returning to the field.".

    Parsons suffered multiple knee injuries, a torn ACL and meniscus, in last season's Week 15 loss at the Denver Broncos. His return comes 346 days after the injuries. Parsons likely won't look like his All-Pro caliber self on every play Wednesday night, but his presence provides a lift to a Packers squad looking to remain on the inside of the postseason picture. At 6-4, Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North behind the Detroit Lions (8-2), Chicago Bears (8-2) and the Minnesota Vikings (7-3), but they enter Week 12 in possession of the conference's No. 7 seed.

    It has been revealed that "I'm so locked in on what's ahead of me and I understand what this game Wednesday means to the organization and I, myself and what it means for playoffs," Parsons stated. "And if I can be out there, I wanna be out there and I'm excited for any time. Because we only got seven more games left, so I wanna capitalize on all those if I can.".

    In a recent development, he is the only player with 12-plus sacks in each of his first five seasons since sacks became an officially tracked individual statistic in 1982, and his 65.0 career sacks rank as the fifth most in a player's first five seasons since 1982. Despite only playing in 14 games last season, Parsons ranked seventh in the NFL in both sacks (12.5) and quarterback pressures (79), which earned him his third first-team All-Pro selection in five seasons.

    In a recent development, green Bay took a nosedive after his injury, losing its final five games of the year, including a wildcard-round defeat at the Chicago Bears. In his absence, the Packers have been the NFL's 16th-ranked scoring defense (22.1 points per game) this season. However, they have produced takeaways (20, the second-most in the NFL) and sacks (29, tied for the seventh-most in the league this season). Having Parsons back on the field should boost the Packers' quarterback pressure rate of 36.2%, which ranks 14th in the NFL.

    "The only thing I'm targeting in a sense of mindset is to win every week to try to uplift this season, change this season around, and do exactly what the Packers brought me here to do," Parsons said. "That's it. That's my only target, and that's to make a run for the playoffs and make guys around me better. That's it.".

    MLB rumors: Mets' Tarik Skubal follow-up, where Blue Jays turn now, plus Yankees, Phillies, Red Sox, more

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1118 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets.
    • It should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m.
    • The Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the Latest York Post.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets. It is far and away the richest pitching contract in history, crushing Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers. The Mets still have other things to address, including adding another starter, but they landed the winter's best free agent.

    It should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the vital offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Monday's hot stove happenings.

    The Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the Latest York Post. Suter will make $3.75 million in 2026, and there's a $3.5 million club option for 2027 with a $250,000 buyout. He is the fourth reliever the Yankees have signed this offseason, joining David Bednar (accepted qualifying offer), Tim Hill, and Jonathan Loáisiga.

    With the bullpen mostly assembled, the Yankees figure to pivot to offense the rest of the offseason. They need a third base upgrade over Ryan McMahon and a right-handed hitting catcher to pair with the lefty-swinging Austin Wells. It seems likely the Yankees will go with Anthony Volpe at second base and Spencer Jones in center field, but those positions can be improved as well.

    According to recent reports, the Mets have agreed to a deal with free agent first baseman Paul Goldschmidt, reports the Fresh York Post. It's a one-year deal worth $8 million, according to The Athletic. He will presumably pair with Jared Young in a first base platoon. We did not rank Goldschmidt, 39, among our top 50 free agents. He accepted a reduced role for the Yankees over the last two seasons and was a valuable clubhouse presence.

    At this point in his career, Goldschmidt is no longer an everyday player, but he remains a solid platoon bat. He hit .317/.402/.572 against lefties over the last two years, compared to .235/.271/.337 against righties. Goldschmidt can still play a nifty first base as well. The Mets received the worst first base production in the sport in 2027. Even late-career Goldschmidt should be an upgrade.

    After missing out on Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays are now believed to be prioritizing Freddy Peralta, according to MLB Network. Toronto has a very good one-two punch in Dylan Cease and José Soriano. Behind them are Spencer Arrighetti, Cody Ponce (returning from a torn ACL), Trey Yesavage, and maybe Jake Bloss and Ricky Tiedemann. There's room for another starter, for sure.

    Peralta, Michael King, and Trevor Rogers are the best available free agent starters now that Skubal has signed. Rogers declined the qualifying offer and is attached to draft pick compensation, which perhaps makes King or Peralta more desirable. Any of the three would boost a Blue Jays rotation that has upside but not much in the way of reliability behind Cease and Soriano.

    Sources indicate that the Dodgers are not expected to aggressively pursue pitching help after losing out on Tarik Skubal, reports The Athletic. They're comfortable letting things play out and seeing what shakes loose among second- and third-tier free agents. As much as the Dodgers would have liked to retain Skubal, they're in a spot where they didn't absolutely need him.

    Despite this year's biceps and knee injuries, Shohei Ohtani is expected to pitch next season. He'll join Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Blake Snell, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto in the rotation. Emmet Sheehan, Gavin Stone, and Justin Wrobleski are next in line, with prospects Jackson Ferris and Christian Zazueta not far away. The Dodgers could use another starter but aren't desperate for one.

    Sources indicate that the Mariners, Padres, and Phillies are among the teams interested in Red Sox outfielder Jarred Duran, according to MassLive. The Red Sox tendered Duran a contract at Friday's deadline and will now look to trade him. The Jake Bauers signing pushed Duran, who had a .266 on-base percentage in 2026, out of the regular lineup. A trade is the logical next step.

    According to recent reports, philadelphia and San Diego badly need outfield help and are obvious fits for Duran. Even if the Mariners manage to re-sign Randy Arozarena, they could use another outfielder, though Duran would be a less-than-stellar fit for a lineup that is already heavily left-handed. Regardless, it seems unlikely Duran will be with the Red Sox by the time Opening Day arrives.

    The Blue Jays, Phillies, and Yankees are considered the favorites for Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports MLB.com. The Cubs and Mets are believed to have interest as well. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers but is not regarded as a strong defender, and it is likely that he will play first base or a corner outfield spot in MLB.

    This past season, Sato, 28 in March, hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs and won Japan's Triple Crown. He is similar to Munetaka Murakami in that he has significant left-handed power, swing-and-miss concerns, and defensive issues. Murakami is a much more patient hitter, however. Sato is an aggressive swinger and is unlikely to walk much or post a strong on-base percentage.

    In a recent development, the Blue Jays offered Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract in the $400 million range before he signed with the Mets, according to The Athletic. Meanwhile, the Dodgers never reached the point of making Skubal an offer, reports ESPN. Los Angeles was known to prefer a short-term, high-dollar contract to a long-term arrangement. Getting Skubal on such a deal always seemed unlikely.

    It has been revealed that as for the Padres, they put forth an offer in the $400 million range but with deferrals that would have lowered the present day value, reports the Latest York Post. Skubal's contract with the Mets includes $30 million in deferred money, which will lower the present day value some, but not significantly. The exact deferrals in San Diego's offer are unknown.

    The Royals and left-handed reliever Caleb Theilbar are in agreement on a one-year deal, per ESPN. Theilbar, 39, was excellent for the Cubs in 2025, but took a step back in 2026, pitching to a 4.86 ERA (87 ERA+) and 1.30 WHIP with 60 strikeouts in 50 innings pitched. He did strand 18 of the 23 runners he inherited, which is an adequate clip for a middle-relief type.

    The Royals recently acquired late-inning lefty José Ferrer in a trade and Daniel Lynch remains in the bullpen, so Thielbar could well be their third option as a lefty in relief.

    #96559. Dwight Howard admits he told Magic not to trade for Stephen Curry before he became 'one of the greatest'

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (963 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Dwight Howard admits he told Magic not to trade for Stephen Curry before he became 'one of the greatest'

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that it is exceedingly rare for teams to have a chance to trade for one of the greatest players in NBA history.
    • The exception to this, bizarrely, has been Stephen Curry.
    • In a recent development, there have been various levels of denial involved in all of these rumors, and we'll never really know all the details, but again, it's not as though we hear about this many botched deals for most of Curry's contemporaries.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that it is exceedingly rare for teams to have a chance to trade for one of the greatest players in NBA history. There were never serious rumors, for instance, about LeBron James or Michael Jordan getting traded. Magic Johnson and Kobe Bryant both issued public trade demands, but pulled back before a deal was consummated. Players like this, for the most part, don't make it to the rumor mill because nobody ever thinks they're seriously available.

    The exception to this, bizarrely, has been Stephen Curry. Though the rumors all died once he hit his prime, there is a rich history of teams that nearly traded for the greatest shooter of all time before he became, well, the greatest shooter of all time. At least three notable deals were reportedly scuttled at the finish line:.

    In a recent development, there have been various levels of denial involved in all of these rumors, and we'll never really know all the details, but again, it's not as though we hear about this many botched deals for most of Curry's contemporaries. Of course, Curry differs from those contemporaries in one key way: he was not a sure thing. James came into the NBA as a preordained star. Anyone claiming they knew what Curry was going to become is almost certainly lying. There was quite a bit of doubt about him early in his career, and that doubt informs our latest entry into the Curry trade chronicles.

    Dwight Howard appeared on the AM Hoops Show on Saturday and shared something few would be eager to admit: he told his former team, the Orlando Magic, not to trade for Stephen Curry. "I wanted to play with Monta Ellis and the Magic wanted to get Steph. The Magic wanted to get Steph and I said no. I said no because I didn't know. I didn't know Steph Curry was going to be one of the greatest," Howard said, regretfully. Asked specifically if the Magic came to him with this, he confirmed. "At the time, Monta was the one who was playing all the minutes," he added.

    Howard did not offer a specific trade proposal or window of time when this could have happened, but two options come to mind. The first would be during the 2010-11 season, when Orlando revamped its team in mid-December by making two blockbuster deals that sent Vince Carter, Rashard Lewis, Marcin Gortat and Mickael Pietrus out while bringing back Gilbert Arenas, Hedo Turkoglu, Jason Richardson and Earl Clark. This would make sense as a period of roster transition, and Ellis was the league leader in minutes that season, averaging more than 40 per game across 80 appearances.

    But Curry was no slouch that season when it came to availability either. He appeared in 74 games and averaged nearly 34 minutes. His availability didn't become a major concern until a year later, when ankle injuries limited him to just 26 games. At that point, his trade value would have been at its lowest, and Howard's leverage with the team would have been at its height. Howard had a player option for the 2012-13 season that he surprisingly exercised... even though the Magic didn't acquire Ellis. Orlando still wound up trading Howard to the Los Angeles Lakers in the summer of 2012.

    Industry observers note that on paper, Curry was perhaps the perfect guard to pair with Howard at his peak. Of course, Curry was and remains the perfect player to pair with just about anyone, but Howard, specifically, tried and failed to mesh with two high-usage star guards in Kobe Bryant and James Harden. Curry's eagerness to play off of the ball would have allowed Howard more post-up possessions, a priority of his at the time even if such plays didn't represent great offense. The team could have run through Howard, but still benefitted enormously from the young Curry's presence before eventually shifting in Curry's direction as Howard aged out of his physical prime.

    Stan Van Gundy was a pioneer in the 3-point revolution, building a four-out lineup around Howard with players like Lewis and Turkoglu. It's tempting to think about what he could have done with a young Curry, especially since Van Gundy would miss another chance to coach him down the line, when he elected to take the Detroit Pistons job in 2014 rather than continuing to pursue Golden State's vacant position.

    Sources indicate that but if there ever really was a window for someone to swoop in and steal Curry, it closed after that third, injury-plagued season. Curry broke out in the 2012-13 season by leading the Warriors back to the playoffs, made his first All-Star team a year later, and then a year after that, he won the first of his two MVP awards and four championships. From that point forward, Golden State had no reason to ever entertain the notion of trading Curry, and Howard, like the Suns, Hornets and Bucks, was left to wonder about what might have been.

    Ironically enough, Howard would get another chance to pair up with Curry in 2013, after Curry had proven himself as Golden State's lead guard. He was a free agent that offseason and met with the Warriors, but seemingly preferred Harden as his running mate, as he signed with the Houston Rockets. The Warriors turned around and used their cap flexibility to add dynasty mainstay Andre Iguodala, an essential part of a team that largely won without high-profile centers like Howard. With the benefit of hindsight, Howard might be one of the most important hidden figures in Golden State's rise to prominence. If he had any inkling of the sort of legend Curry was destined to become, the Warriors dynasty may never have happened.

    Frankfurt’s pressing adjustments secure victory over Galatasaray – MH

    📅 22 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1358 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 22.09.2025 in den Kategorien Champions League mit 1 Kommentar.
    • Eintracht Frankfurt won their opening Champions League matchday with a 5-1 victory over Galatasaray Istanbul.
    • Frankfurt started, as usual, in a nominal 4-2-3-1.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 22.09.2025 in den Kategorien Champions League mit 1 Kommentar.

    Eintracht Frankfurt won their opening Champions League matchday with a 5-1 victory over Galatasaray Istanbul. After about ten minutes, Frankfurt were trailing 0-1, but thanks in part to adjusted pressing, they were able to turn the game around. What follows is an aspect analysis of Frankfurt’s attacking press against the Istanbul side’s build-up play.

    Frankfurt started, as usual, in a nominal 4-2-3-1. Ahead of the two midfielders Chaibi and Larsson, Uzun operated in the No. 10 role. On the left flank, winger Knauff played in front of left-back Brown. When dropping into a deeper defensive press, this structure shifted into a 4-4-2, with Burkardt and either Uzun or Knauff forming the first pressing line. In the transition to the attacking press, they shifted man-oriented as usual.

    Sources indicate that galatasaray also began in a nominal 4-2-3-1. In possession, their structure changed depending on the depth of their build-up, forming something like a 3-2-5 or 4-2-4 through the positioning of the full-backs. Width on the right side was provided by winger Sané, and on the left by full-back Elmalı. Left winger Akgün frequently moved inside, acting as a kind of “free player.” Meanwhile, right-back Sallai tucked in slightly in higher possession phases to help form a back three in the build-up.

    It has been revealed that galatasaray’s build-up was characterized by frequent rotations. Their basic reference point was the previously described 3-2-5. From this shape, they consistently sought positional interchanges in order to manipulate the opponent’s man-marking in the pressing phase. On the left side, Elmalı, who provided width, was able to vary his height. In deeper build-up phases, he often dropped further back, while he also regularly positioned himself on the last line. Winger Akgün was tasked with creating central overloads and repeatedly moved inside, at times even drifting over to the right side. In response to the full-back pushing high, the left holding midfielder, Lemina, rotated into the left-back position. Striker Yılmaz, in turn, shifted into the left half-space when the full-back stayed deeper and the winger dropped centrally.

    Galatasaray’s left-sided rotations force Frankfurt’s pressing players into constant reorientation.

    In a recent development, the purpose of these rotations was to manipulate man-marking and tie down specific Frankfurt players. Because winger Akgün frequently dropped into central areas, the two centre-backs, Koch and Theate, were occupied. Akgün positioned himself in front of striker Yılmaz in order to stretch the last line and create 1v1 opportunities. This produced a variety of different build-up structures, which required Frankfurt to constantly reorient themselves. For example, if Elmalı pushed high, he had to be tracked by Collins, and Galatasaray’s four attacking players tied down Frankfurt’s entire back line. This significantly complicated Frankfurt’s transition into man-marking, as the positioning of the forwards forced centre-back Theate to cover long distances during handovers.

    Since all players in the back line are occupied, defensive handovers become more difficult.

    In a recent development, frankfurt’s blueprint, as in previous matches, was to shift into man-marking from a +1 overload through the handover of the opponents’ centre-backs and full-backs. The advantage of this approach is that spaces on and behind the last line can initially be secured, while the risk of a long ball leading to a 1v1 situation is minimized by having an additional covering player.

    At the same time, after steering the opponent’s attack, the transition into man-marking could be executed to apply maximum pressure on the ball carrier. Depending on the opponent’s structure and build-up sequences, Frankfurt adapted their pressing schemes. For instance, they could vary the distance to their opponents during the pressing jump: larger distances allowed for greater security in coverage, while smaller distances created more immediate pressure.

    In a recent development, galatasaray tried to make these handover moments as difficult as possible for Frankfurt by forcing the distances at the moment of transition into man-marking to become as large as possible. The aforementioned rotations, for example, forced Theate into long runs to pick up winger Sané, so that Brown could then jump out to the still unmarked and deeper-positioned right-back of Galatasaray.

    Because of Galatasaray’s attackers’ positioning, Theate and Brown are forced into long pressing runs. On top of that, Theate finds himself caught between two opponents due to the rotations.

    Galatasaray also tried to open up the center through certain rotations, aiming to draw Frankfurt’s midfielders out of central areas. Frankfurt tracked man-to-man with Larsson on half-space player Gündogan and Uzun on the deeper right-sided pivot Torreira. Depending on the side of build-up, Chaibi was prepared to jump onto the more advanced pivot, Lemina. Because Lemina often rotated into the full-back position, Doan frequently picked him up, leaving Chaibi or Collins (depending on the movements of Akgün and Elmalı) unexpectedly without a direct opponent. At the same time, Gündogan and Torreira sometimes rotated in opposite directions, which created difficulties for Frankfurt in terms of handovers in central areas.

    Because Frankfurt found it increasingly difficult to press Galatasaray’s build-up through their usual handover approach, from around the 15th minute they opted for tighter marking distances to transition more quickly into full man-marking. Brown pushed up directly, Theate went straight onto Sané, while Collins and Koch marked the two remaining forwards. This created a 3v3 situation on the last line. Although this increased the pressure on Galatasaray and led to more turnovers in their build-up, it also raised the risk against long balls due to isolated 1v1s. Time and again, Galatasaray managed to exploit this by sending strong dribblers like Sané into such spacious 1v1 situations. Even so, the tighter marking distances resulted in a much more balanced game with more frequent ball recoveries.

    In the 30th minute, Frankfurt used a longer stoppage to make more significant pressing adjustments. Winger Knauff no longer pressed Galatasaray’s right centre-back but instead oriented himself toward full-back Sallai. This allowed Brown to stay on Sané, and Theate no longer had to make long runs out wide to cover him. At the same time, it was no longer problematic if all four defenders were tied up, as they no longer needed to jump out of the back line. The free centre-back was now primarily pressed by Uzun, who used his cover shadow to block passing lanes into pivot Torreira. Galatasaray’s build-up on the right side could then be pressed man-to-man through ball-oriented shifting. To this end, Chaibi stepped onto Uzun’s original opponent, Torreira, and the far-side Doan also moved into the ball-near center.

    Industry observers note that frankfurt’s pressing adjustments: With no need to shift across the last line anymore, Frankfurt gains situationally much better access with less risk. These changes spark the turnaround in the match.

    Sources indicate that the pressing adjustments led to significantly better situational access and, at the same time, to much stronger defensive security. Frankfurt were able to use the resulting ball recoveries to establish longer possession phases, which gave them a more dominant style of play. One such spell of possession resulted in the 2-1 lead shortly before halftime. Immediately afterwards, a ball recovery from the adjusted attacking press led to a free kick, which in turn produced the 3-1 at the break.

    In the opening 30 minutes, Galatasaray were able to cause Frankfurt problems, thanks in part to a very elusive build-up play that challenged Frankfurt’s typical pressing approach with its reliance on handover moments. Frankfurt’s adjustments, however, proved perfectly suited to applying pressure more easily while also improving defensive cover. The short interruption of play came at just the right time for Toppmöller and his coaching staff to implement the necessary measures. As a result, the pressing changes were decisive for Frankfurt’s eventual 5-1 victory and a successful start to their Champions League campaign.

    #96553. Ranking NBA's biggest winners and losers of the week: Knicks hit their stride, while Celtics take step back

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1689 w)
    📖 Baca

    Ranking NBA's biggest winners and losers of the week: Knicks hit their stride, while Celtics take step back

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1689 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Let's call the last seven days the NBA's first parity week of the season.
    • Industry observers note that the Western Conference is similarly crunched.
    • You're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the New Orleans Pelicans, aren't you?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Let's call the last seven days the NBA's first parity week of the season. Take a look at the standings right now. The No. 2 through the No. 6 seeds in the Eastern Conference standings all have exactly six losses, and while the Philadelphia 76ers hold a three-game lead for the No. 1 seed, they've done so behind a preposterous 12-0 clutch record. When they regress to the mean, we seem destined for an Eastern Conference packed like sardines.

    Industry observers note that the Western Conference is similarly crunched. The San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers sit atop the standings with identical 14-3 records... but seeds 3-9 are all separated by no more than two games. Even the Sacramento Kings got a win this week! The NBA has spent years tinkering in order to create parity, and right now, at least it's getting it. With that unofficial week of parity in the books, let's crown some winners and losers from the last seven days.

    You're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the New Orleans Pelicans, aren't you? That'd be the easy starting point. We could just as easily kick things off with Luka Dončić's shooting dip, as he has quietly shot roughly 41-31-82 in his past five games, bringing his ridiculous offensive numbers down to slightly more mortal levels and making Wembanyama, for now, the slight MVP betting favorite. Totally reasonable. They're both contributors to his excellent week.

    Industry observers note that neither stands up to what Wembanyama did against the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday. He shunked. That's a word that didn't exist when we woke up on Thursday. It is now, hilariously, a signature moment of Wembanyama's young career. He has apparently dunked so often, so violently that he suffered a hand injury that compelled him to try, and succeed, to shoot a jump shot at the rim.

    It has been revealed that did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    The MVP race is for the season. The ridiculous numbers are for the history books. The shunk wins the week. Any time you suffer and overcome a dunking-related injury by inventing a new form of scoring, you win the week.

    Sources indicate that the champs have won five in a row and are 11-3 overall since their 0-3 start, but this isn't as simple as the Knicks suddenly looking like the Knicks again. Many of the early season problems are still persisting. Mikal Bridges hit the game-winner on Friday and still shot 3-of-12 on Sunday. Josh Hart missed all four of his 3-pointers on Sunday and is below 26% shooting from deep so far this season. The starters, as a group, are still getting outscored by almost 13 points per 100 possessions after struggling mightily in the past two regular seasons.

    Yet they just keep winning. There are obvious basketball reasons for that. Karl-Anthony Towns is getting every rebound, making every shot, and has readopted the playmaking hub role he thrived in throughout the postseason, particularly when it comes to assisting Jalen Brunson. The bench is thriving. Landry Shamet is shooting better than 45% on 3s and Deuce McBride isn't far behind. Tyler Kolek has a 61-to-9 assist-to-turnover ratio.

    But there's something deeper here, a resilience and versatility that developed over last season's championship run that is sustaining thus far this season. OG Anunoby has missed the past two games. Towns missed the Blazers game. Bridges and Hart play most of some games and only parts of others because of their early season struggles. Yet Mike Brown just keeps pulling the right levers, and the Knicks just keep figuring it out. Championships can bring about this certainty. The Knicks aren't quite themselves yet, but they have an internalized confidence that came from dominating the playoff crucible a year ago that's paying off handsomely right now.

    Recent findings suggest that it's hard to tell what we've seen from the Heat thus far this season that really deserves scrutiny. They started 0-4 in part because opponents weren't missing any 3s. They've gone 8-2 since, but they haven't beaten a single notable, fully healthy opponent during their active seven-game winning streak. No Evan Mobley against the Cleveland Cavaliers. No Jalen Duren against the Detroit Pistons. No Amen Thompson against the Houston Rockets. No... basically anyone against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday, though in fairness, Giannis Antetokounmpo missed that game himself. Miami is something of a Rorschach test so far. You're going to see what you're predisposed to seeing.

    But if we're going to panic during the shooting luck-induced losing streak, we're going to have to acknowledge the positives during the winning streak. The maligned Heat offense ranks in the top five over their past 10 games largely because Klay Thompson is shooting like Klay Thompson again and Giannis Antetokounmpo never stopped dunking like Giannis Antetokounmpo. Their core lineups featuring Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo are deterring rim attempts and giving up basically no corner 3s. Andrew Wiggins looks more like Andrew Wiggins since moving to the bench. As tempted as I was to give the third slot to the player development coaches for the Memphis Grizzlies after Cam Spencer's breakout 26-point game against Cleveland, the seven-game Miami winning streak gets the nod.

    The Celtics were too clever by a half with their lineup decisions this weekend. They sat Jayson Tatum and Derrick White against the hapless Kings and then sat Paul George in the second half of that back-to-back against the Stephen Curry-less Golden State Warriors. They lost both very winnable games by a single point when they probably could have ensured a split and maybe even a sweep by aligning the rest. Throw in a 17-point blown lead to the Denver Nuggets and allowing a 40-point fourth quarter against the Orlando Magic and the previously 11-2 Celtics lost all four of their games this week. They're back with the Eastern Conference pack.

    Recent findings suggest that it's too early to draw any real conclusions, just as it was too early to crown them Eastern Conference favorites when they were throttling the Sixers two weeks ago, but this week was a reminder of some of the cracks here. Their best player is coming off of a torn Achilles, and their second- and third-best players are in their 30s and have to be managed carefully throughout the season. You can get away with never getting to the basket as a team when you're an elite 3-point shooting outfit. The Celtics haven't been this season, and we're now in Year 2 of Derrick White's 3-point drought (and, for that matter, arguably Year 3 of Jayson Tatum's). Mitchell Robinson will put together a few good stretches and then regress back into the mess he's been for most of the season. Boston has been nearly 22 points stronger per 100 possessions with him off the floor this season.

    The Celtics, given their playing style and roster makeup, are vulnerable to the ebbs and flows of an 82-game season. When everyone's available and they're making their shots, they're going to look unbeatable. This week is what happens when they're not, and considering how frequently that's been the case for them in the playoffs, it's something the Celtics are going to have to learn to play through if they hope to make it through this crowded East.

    Slowly but surely, the NBA's cellar dwellers are starting to come around. The Utah Jazz won twice this week. The Chicago Bulls have won three times since Caleb Wilson went down, and they pushed the Denver Nuggets to overtime on Sunday. The Kings got win No. 2 on Saturday, but also pushed the Los Angeles Lakers to the brink on Friday. There is still a whole lot of misery at the bottom of the standings, but all of these teams can find small pockets of optimism.

    Industry observers note that not the Bucks, who are now the NBA's last one-win team and owners of a 13-game losing streak. One of those losses came against Miami this week as their former franchise player, Antetokounmpo, throttled them for three quarters before they made the final score look respectable in the fourth quarter. They have the NBA's worst defense comfortably. Beyond a three-game stretch in which second-year guard Kasparas Jakučionis averaged 21 points per game, it's simply been a miserable season in Milwaukee, and it's one that could get worse any day now as the NBA investigates potential salary cap circumvention involving Gary Trent Jr. We all knew the Bucks would struggle with post-Giannis life, but this is worse than anyone could have imagined.

    According to recent reports, tyrese Haliburton has played four games this season at a roughly All-Star level. The Indiana Pacers are now 3-10 in all other contests, and ESPN reported Friday that Haliburton is set to miss at least another few weeks with a left hamstring strain. This is after a 19-win season played entirely without Haliburton a year ago. At this point, obvious as it sounds, it's simply become clear that the Pacers can't win consistently without their best player. That was obvious in a playoff context, but the regular-season implications here are starting to add up.

    Indiana is already six games out of a top-six Eastern Conference seed. Even when Haliburton gets back, he's probably not going to be perfectly healthy for the entire rest of the season just given his own history of durability concerns. The East's bottom four teams are thankfully so dreadful that there's probably a floor of No. 11 here, but Indiana will eventually have to pass someone -- presumably the Washington Wizards, perhaps someone else who gets bitten by the injury bug -- just to make it back into the Play-In Tournament picture. Even if they're there, their road to and through the playoffs becomes enormously precarious. It doesn't matter how dangerous you are in a playoff setting if you can't actually survive the regular season and make it there. It's too early to say that's where Indiana is headed, but the danger is very real.

    Tech Report: 2027 NBA Draft Substantial Board: Quentin Coleman's meteoric rise, Tyran Stokes stays at No. 1, returners boost stock

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1705 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open.
    • But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Substantial Board.
    • It has been revealed that inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open. There are still eight months to go before Adam Silver steps up to the podium to announce the first pick. Nothing has been decided yet. In fact, there's probably only about ten players total that can confidently say they expect to be a first-round pick at this point. Everything else is yet to be determined.

    But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Substantial Board.

    It has been revealed that inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects. They're still building their lists, sorting them into tiers, and will spend the coming months trying to establish their order.

    That's the biggest difference between those front offices and the public discourse about the draft. The fans want answers now, and the Twitter scouts are quick to make bold statements in hopes of saying they were right first. The experts who actually do this for a living recognize that the sole goal is to be right on draft night, and doing that requires them to not jump to any early conclusions.

    Recent findings suggest that that's all critical context to understanding this big board upgrade, which is, at best, a way too early look at the most relevant prospects. It should be interpreted in tiers. There are probably five or six prospects competing for the top of the draft, but that list could change. Maybe 11 who should feel good about their chances to be first-round picks. Everything beyond that is simply a battle that will continue to play out over the course of the next 8 months. Let's dive into the biggest storylines after three weeks of college basketball action.

    Recent findings suggest that I got a first-hand look at Stokes last week at the Player's Era 8 in Las Vegas. He went down with a contusion midway through his first game, sat out the second, and returned to drop 22 points and 11 rebounds in the final. In totality, the signs of extreme growth that have characterized his early season play continued to be evident in Vegas. He was far and away the most talented player in high school basketball a year ago, but had developed a history of not living up to his potential, or at least not impacting winning to the degree that someone with his talent should. So, coming into his year at Kansas, the eyeballs were more about his maturity, reliability, and approach. Answering those questions has gone about as well as it possibly could so far. He's not only been engaged and impactful, but he's shown connectivity with Bill Self that makes him look coachable. He's also not gotten easily derailed by adversity, which is a reassuring data point.

    In a recent development, to be clear, for as good as he's been, there's still plenty of room for improvement. In high school, he had an instinctive way of improvising his way to the rim. In college, he's found that isn't quite as easy, even with someone like Tre Kaufman-Renn regularly clearing the way for him anytime he comes charging at the rim. So, while he's over-dribbling at times, his playmaking is real, he's asserted himself as a rebounder, his shooting is progressing, and he's starting to use his size in the post.

    It has been revealed that the bottom line is this: most teams are looking for a potential alpha-type creator with the first pick. Stokes is your best bet in the 2027 cycle, by a relatively large margin at this point, but it's still too early to say he's a lock to go number one. I'd put that at about 70% at this point. Getting to the finish line will require him to continue trending in the right direction, making sure teams are comfortable with their due diligence in the pre-draft process, and also leaving open the possibility for someone else to emerge in the coming months.

    Speaking of ascending prospects, no one has moved the needle more in the first three weeks of the season than Illinois' freshman Quentin Coleman. But for those who track draft prospects 365 days a year, the last three weeks are just a short spurt in what has been a rapid rise over the course of the last 15 months.

    In the 2025 EYBL season, Coleman averaged 11.8 points. 5.1 rebounds and 2.4 assists for a Brad Beal Elite team that won the Peach Jam Championship. To put it plainly, he was a role player, albeit a valuable one, on a team that was built around current Arkansas freshman JJ Andrews and utilized Trey Pearson, who is presently a freshman at High Point, as their primary ball-handler and distributor.

    It has been revealed that as soon as Coleman's high school season began, though, we immediately saw signs of growth. Those signs continued throughout the course of the year, and he skyrocketed the rankings in the process. He also decommitted from Wake Forest and took a much bigger NIL payday from Illinois. While he finished with five-star status, it was immediately clear at the USA Basketball trials in May that even that was too low.

    According to recent reports, since arriving at Illinois, Coleman has continued the pattern of exceeding expectations. His skill level, feel for the game, defensive instincts, and nose for the ball are all as impressive as expected. The physical transition has been easier than expected. He's continued to develop more burst, physicality, and, as a result, playmaking.

    Sources indicate that at the moment, he's moved all the way up to No. 4 on the CBS's current 2027 NBA Draft Substantial Board, but we're not going to put a cap on what he could do given the unprecedented growth we've witnessed over the last 15 months.

    There were a number of prospects who had a chance to be first-round picks in last year's draft, who opted to return to college basketball. While most, if not all, of them are probably making more money in college this year than they would have in the NBA, they are also making strides with their game, and in the process, helping their draft stock in what is widely viewed as a weaker draft than last year's.

    We've been bullish on Amari Allen's chances of helping himself given his new on-ball role at Alabama, and so far, he's done just that. The 16 points, 6 assists, and 5 rebounds per game on 52/50/82 shooting showcases both the versatility and shooting gains we were banking on. Most of all, though, it's his decision-making with the ball that has been glaring. His usage has gone way up, and his turnovers have gone way down. He has recorded 30 assists against just three turnovers through the first five games of the season. Add his hyper-competitiveness to the equation, and he's certainly helping himself.

    According to recent reports, arizona massive man Motiejus Krivas looked like an NBA-ready defender last year. This year, it's been more of the same. He's massive, even by NBA standards, at 7-foot-2 and 260 pounds, but deceptively versatile and very smart with his angles. We're also seeing definite growth offensively, particularly with his skill set facing the basket. Last week's 18-point, 12-rebound, 4-block performance against UConn was one that captured all of his value, and a game that scouts will undoubtedly revisit.

    Meanwhile, his teammate, Ivan Kharchenkov, has gone from a defensive role player to Arizona's featured scorer, and is putting up nearly 23 points, 8 rebounds, and 5 assists per game. To put it plainly, he's been as good of a two-way player as there is in the country, and now looks like he could be trending towards the draft lottery.

    In a recent development, florida's Thomas Haugh had a chance to be a mid-first-round pick last June, but the variable that gave many scouts pause was his shooting. This year, he's shooting it with much more confidence and rhythm, making 18 of his 34 attempts through his first five games. Simultaneously, he's continuing to do all the little things that made him so intriguing in the first place with his motor, physicality, rebounding, and defensive versatility.

    Speaking of shooting, Braylon Mullins is establishing himself as one of the nation's premier shooters, as expected, despite the fact that he's clearly not 100% healthy. Through his first five games, he's made 19 threes on 50 attempts, but it's been the types of shots that have really stood out. He's running all over the court, flying off screens, and making threes on the move, all while being the focal point of opposing defenses. In short, Mullins is making the type of tough shots that translate to the next level, despite not having his typical ability to separate.

    One of the defining characteristics of the national 2026 recruiting class was the number of prospects who had glaring potential, but had yet to put it all together. That list included the likes of Duke's Cameron Williams,  Ohio State's Anthony Thompson, Maryland's Baba Oladotun, Christian Collins,  Adonis Rayliff and Darius Ratliff, all at USC. Nevertheless, almost all of them commanded the type of recruitment and correlating financial commitment that suggested programs were willing to invest in their development.

    So far In t those investments have not resulted in the types of gains we had hoped for. The Ratliffs, Adonis in particular, have demonstrated some flashes, while Collins has only recently been cleared. Williams and Oladotun are barely in the rotation, and Thompson is playing, but not making the type of impact that anyone hoped.

    According to recent reports, now, despite the lack of immediate return at the college level, most NBA decision-makers are still playing the long game, so I wouldn't expect any of these guys to be given up on just yet. Nevertheless, their early struggles did have to be accounted for on the big board, which is why many of them are now outside the top 30.

    #96538. The Issue of Passivity – MX
